title: Protocol and Gravity
premise: Ines Thornbury, a former insurance investigator turned cargo hauler, has spent five years hiding in contested orbits after falsifying the report of an accident that killed his sister. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, he realizes the anomaly matches the impossible accident he buried—and that someone is using his old case files to trace him. Racing a rival salvage crew and the decay of a dying relay's signal, he must reach dead space to confront the AI archive that holds both the truth of his sister's death and her uploaded memories. In the end, Ines chooses to broadcast the truth at the cost of the archive, letting his sister finally die so the living can be free.
about_author: Jude Kavanagh is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about people whose jobs are to explain what should never have happened.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Ines, hauling ore through contested orbits, experiences the system-wide gravity flicker and nearly loses his ship. His POV establishes his careful invisibility and the routines he uses to stay untraceable. The beat is unease: the flicker feels familiar, like something he once investigated and chose not to understand.

chapters.title: The Claim That Wouldn't Close
chapters.summary: A message arrives from Meridian Assurance reopening Case 77-Kestrel—the accident that killed his sister Ada—flagged by the same anomaly signature as the flicker. Ines's POV; he burns five years of careful records to cover his tracks. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing as panic, revealing he falsified the original report.

chapters.title: Cargo of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ines takes one last legitimate contract to fund a run to dead space, meeting stowaway engineer Priya Okonkwo, who recognizes the flicker data as a handshake protocol, not a malfunction. Dual tension: she wants the truth, he wants it buried. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual leverage.

chapters.title: What the Salvage Crew Knows
chapters.summary: At a waystation, Ines learns rival salvager Corvo Dane is also racing toward the edge relay, carrying stolen fragments of Ada's case file. Priya decodes a fragment: Ada's death involved an experimental memory archive called Loom. Beat: Ines realizes hiding made him predictable; he must move first.

chapters.title: Dead Space Is Not Empty
chapters.summary: Crossing into dead space, the ship suffers cascading failures—Loom's signal is warping local physics. Ines's POV alternates with recovered log entries from Ada, alive-voiced and funny, deepening his grief. Beat: the past becomes more present than the journey; love against duty sharpens.

chapters.title: Corvo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dane intercepts them, offering partnership: he wants Loom's value; he knows Ines is Ada's brother and will expose him otherwise. Ines accepts under duress while Priya secretly plans betrayal of both men for the scientific record. Beat: trust fraying on all sides; the race becomes three-way.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They reach the derelict relay and find Loom's archive intact, tended by a caretaker subroutine modeled on Ada's final hours. Ines speaks with a reconstruction of his sister who remembers everything—including his falsified report. Beat: devastating confrontation; forgiveness he cannot accept.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Dane seizes the relay core to sell Loom whole; Priya sabotages him to force public disclosure. The station begins failing as Loom destabilizes, threatening to repeat the nine-second flicker at catastrophic scale. Beat: climax ignition—Ines must choose between preserving Ada's ghost and stopping the collapse.

chapters.title: Let Her Go
chapters.summary: Climax: Ines chooses to purge Loom, broadcasting its full contents—truths about the accident, the corporate experiment, his own lie—system-wide before destroying the core. Ada's reconstruction thanks him. Dane escapes empty-handed; Priya transmits corroboration. Beat: grief transmuted into release; duty finally bent toward love.

chapters.title: Gravity, Holding
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ines testifies rather than flees, surrendering his investigator's license but keeping his ship. Priya stays aboard as partner; the system reels from the revelations but no second flicker comes. Final beat: quiet resolution—he stops running, carries memory instead of being carried by it.
